title: Spotter probe integration & synthetic workload harness
content:
Purpose:

This doc outlines a lightweight "Spotter" probe and synthetic workload harness for routine serving-runtime performance checks. The goal is a low-friction, repeatable way to snapshot hotspot signals across model sizes and sequence lengths, integrate those snapshots into perf CI, and automatically surface regressions in flamegraphs and call-trace deltas.

Background / motivation:

We currently have heavier profiling playbooks (full tracer captures, eBPF flamegraph collection) that are excellent for deep-debug sessions but are expensive to run frequently. Teams ask for something between: cheap, deterministic probes that run on every perf CI run and a richer capture triggered on anomaly. "Spotter" is the minimal probe: small runtime sampler + synthetic workload templates + automated baseline comparison.

High-level design:

- Spotter probe: a lightweight, non-intrusive process that samples stack traces at configurable intervals (default 1000Hz aggregated to 50Hz effective) and writes compressed stack-stacks for quick flamegraph generation. Implementation options: simple perf_stat wrapper or an eBPF userspace sampler (bcc/bpftrace) depending on node privileges.
- Synthetic harness: set of small end-to-end inference workloads (short-chat, long-context, streaming-1s) that exercise decode path, KV cache hot-paths, and cache-miss code paths. Workloads are deterministic and seeded.
- CI integration: Spotter runs as a post-deploy stage in perf CI (parallel to latency/throughput tests). Artifacts (compressed stacks, metadata) are uploaded to an artifact store and compared against baseline.
- Triage automation: a script that computes top-10 delta stacks and posts summary (SVG flamegraph + text diffs) to PR and perf dashboard. If regression > threshold, fail CI or open a ticket automatically.

Spotter probe implementation notes:

- Minimal requirements: rootless capture preferred. Two modes:
  1) rootless: use user-space sampling via pthread_sigqueue or sharableptrace-lite (fallback) to capture program counters from top-level threads. Lower fidelity but safe for shared infra.
  2) privileged: use perf record -g --freq=999 or bpftrace script capturing ustack(uid) for top callers; higher fidelity.
- Output format: folded stacks (flamegraph.pl compatible) gzipped and named metadata: model, image, seq_len, batch, run-id, timestamp. Example filename: spotter-folded-bert-2k-1b-20251102T1401.gz
- Sampling policy: default 1ms sample interval for decode hot-paths; for KV-heavy scenarios allow 250us sampling for short bursts (config param).

Synthetic workload templates (examples):

1) short-chat (chatty user): 512-token prompt, stop tokens, streaming enabled, temperature=0.2, beam=1, 4 parallel requests for 30s. Purpose: steady-state decode CPU path.
2) long-context-attn (context stress): 8192 tokens left-padded with random token ids to simulate long KV cache warmups; single request to measure attention kernel scaling.
3) kv-evict (cache-churn): sequence of requests that intentionally invalidates prefix cache by varying prompt prefixes; repeated windowed fetches to trigger KV update paths.
4) small-emb (embedding): 1k short texts batched in 3s window to surface batching & queueing logic.

CI job sketch (GitHub Actions / Jenkins snippet):

- job: perf-spotter
  runs-on: perf-runner
  steps:
    - checkout
    - deploy-to-test-node (image tagged from PR)
    - run-synthetic-harness --workload short-chat --duration 30 --parallel 4
    - run-spotter --mode=rootless --out artifacts/$RUN_ID
    - gzip artifacts/* && upload-artifact artifacts/$RUN_ID
    - run-compare --baseline s3://perf-baselines/spotter/latest.json --candidate artifacts/$RUN_ID --report artifacts/$RUN_ID/report.json
    - if report.json.regression_score > 0.05: post-pr-comment and mark-failure

Automated comparison & triage heuristics:

- Metrics derived from stacks: proportion of samples in top N stacks, entropy change, and cumulative delta for decode/kernels.
- Score = weighted(sum of positive deltas for target hotspots) / baseline-sample-count. Thresholds: 3% (info), 5% (warning/fail), 12% (urgent).
- When threshold exceeded, attach: baseline flamegraph SVG, candidate flamegraph SVG, top 15 delta stacks with ids, and a short description of likely subsystem (e.g., "quantized matmul kernel increased 4.2x samples").

Flamegraph generation flow (fast path):

1) folded stacks gz -> flamegraph.pl --title "spotter $WORKLOAD $MODEL" > out.svg
2) render small PNG preview for PR thumbnail (convert -resize 1200x400)
3) compute text diffs by aggregating by function prefix and computing delta percentages

Collector alternatives and tradeoffs:

- perf record: high fidelity, needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN or perf_event_open fine-grained permissions. Good for nightly or dedicated nodes.
- bpftrace / eBPF: lower overhead, high resolution; requires kernel+infra support. Good for dedicated perf fleet.
- user-space sampler: least privileged, easiest to run in hosted-dedicated hybrids; lower precision around inlined frames.

Data retention and storage strategy:

- Keep last 30 spotter runs per model in s3; archive monthly snapshots (30-day) and permanent baselines for releases. Compressed stacks are small (200KB–2MB) but flame SVGs are ~150–400KB.
- Add lifecycle rules: delete raw folded stacks after 90 days, keep aggregated baselines and alerts for 365 days.

Observability & dashboarding:

- Perf dashboard tile: spotter-regressions (time-series of regression_score per model per last-commit), top failing functions heatmap, and links to artifacts.
- Alerts: Ops slack channel #perf-alerts when regression_score > 0.05 for mainline branches. For customer-facing dedicated images, send alert to #dedicated-ops with higher threshold (0.03).

Runbook (quick triage):

- Step 1: review the PR flamegraph diff attachment. If the delta is in third-party kernel libm or BLAS, escalate to NPQ team.
- Step 2: reproduce locally with privileged perf record on identical image; if reproduce, collect full perf.data and traces.
- Step 3: bisect the change if the regression map points to specific git SHAs (use CI bisect harness).
- Step 4: if non-reproducible, schedule nightly deep-capture (eBPF) to correlate with transient infra noise.

Open questions / TODOs:

- Decide default sample interval across all models (tradeoff between sensitivity and CI runtime).
- Finalize rootless stack capture approach for hosted nodes without perf privileges. Can we ship a tiny ptrace helper?
- Add support for GPU sampling (NVIDIA CUPTI / nvprof alternatives) to include GPU kernels in the flamegraphs.
- Integrate with cost model: estimate per-spotter-run credit cost and gating policy for on-demand vs nightly.

Next steps (short-term roadmap):

- Spike: implement a reference spotter in Go (unix signal stack snapshot) and validate against perf record on 3 workloads (1 week).
- CI pilot: wire spotter into perf CI for model-staging images (2 weeks).
- Dashboard: add reporting tile & Slack integration (2–3 weeks).

Notes to self / scratchpad:

- Keep workload fixtures under infra/tests/spotter-fixtures to allow reproducible seeds.
- Use run-id naming convention: model-workload-seq-batch-runid for easy grouping in S3.
- Potential name: "spotter" vs "spotter-probe" — short name wins in scripts.

References:

- flamegraph.pl (Brendan Gregg)
- bpftrace examples for ustack and profile
- internal: SERV-2930 perf CI baseline storage design
